name: g_crc32Table
comment: Standard IEEE 802.3 (reflected, polynomial 0xEDB88320) CRC-32 lookup table: 256 u32 entries, 1024 bytes. std_Crc32_InitTable copies it into the caller's buffer and the save-code helpers use it to build/verify the save checksum. The first entry is 0x00000000, which is why an image scan reports the object as zero-initialised.
evidence: std_Crc32_InitTable (0x005F08DC) does std_memcpy(stack, 0x0072EB3C, 0x400) then std_memcpy(dst, stack, 0x400); all 256 words match the standard reflected table (0x00000000, 0x77073096, 0xEE0E612C, 0x990951BA, 0x076DC419, ...); callers are SaveCode_GenerateCheckDigits (0x005F0408) and SaveCode_DecodeAndVerify (0x005EFE3C); literal slot 0x005F0920.

name: g_moLiveAllocatorOutOfMemoryMessage
comment: Allocator out-of-memory report text: "MoLive::Allocator: not enough memory to allocate %d bytes !!!\n" (62 characters plus the NUL). Every allocation helper passes it to allocator vtable slot +8 together with the failed byte count, so this is the message a modder sees when the game runs out of memory.
evidence: Exact NUL-terminated string at 0x00735154 (62 chars + NUL = 63 bytes). std_SlotVector_Reallocate (0x00710170) and std_RbTree_AcquireNode (0x0070C414) call (*alloc->vt[2])(alloc, 0x00735154, size) immediately after (*alloc->vt[0])(size) returned NULL; also used by MoLive_Reader_DecodePacket (0x005ED154) and std_SlotVector_AppendRange. Literal slots 0x005EE394, 0x0070C524, 0x0071016C and 0x007102F8 all hold this address.

name: g_formatStringTag128
comment: Class word stored at offset 0 of the narrow (char) format-string temporary built by maybe_std_String_FormatCtorA (0x006F0998): the object is {this word; char buf[128]} and vsnprintf (0x001001C4) fills the buffer at +4. The 16-byte slot is all zero in the retail image and no code calls through it, so it only tags the class; the capacity is what distinguishes it from the other format-string classes.
evidence: Stored by `*out = 0x00781FA0` in maybe_std_String_FormatCtorA (0x006F0998, literal slot inside the body); the wrapper at 0x006F0990 does `push {r0-r3}` and sets r1=128 (buffer capacity); it zeroes the first element with `strb r0,[r4,#4]` and tail-calls vsnprintf (0x001001C4) with r0=out+4, r2=fmt, r3=&first vararg. Callers (1): Ui_GridTextWindow_InitPanes - they pass out+4 on as a pane name / text. The 16-byte slot at 0x00781FA0 is all zero in code.decompressed.bin and sits in the .rodata vtable area (neighbouring slots 0x007815D8 / 0x00781D94 / 0x007822A0 hold real code pointers).

comment: Display order of the 31 item bag categories: g_itemBagCategoryOrder[category] is the slot index the bag UI shows that category in. Built once at startup by 0x0017B994 and read by the bag/equipment sort comparator so items are grouped in the same order the bag screen uses.
evidence: 0x0017B994 loops i in 0..0x1E, calls 0x0066B0E4(work+0x24A98, i) and stores `*(int *)(0x007C6E7C + category * 4) = i` when the returned category is < 0x1F, so the table is 31 s32 entries indexed by category. std_less_itemId8 (0x0071428C) compares `*(int *)(0x007C6E7C + classB*4) <= *(int *)(0x007C6E7C + classA*4)` after bounding both class bytes (item record +4) to < 0x1F; the same table is used by std_less_itemName8, std_insertion_sort_itemId8/Name8 and std_push_heap_itemId8/Name8. BSS, so it is zero in the image and filled at runtime; literal slots 0x0017BA00, 0x007143A0, 0x0071449C, 0x0071618C, 0x00716360, 0x00716ED4, 0x00717104.
